To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
North Korea’s food production is highly dependent on agricultural resources, and that food balance will improve if a more pro market oriented economic policy is adopted.
North Korean food production is negatively correlated with the level of agricultural resources and with a pro-military economic policy.
North Korea is a country in which food production decreases along the decreasing rate of input factors and with a more pro-militarist economic policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
food supply and demand in the autarkic economy of North Korea.
food balance in North Korea.
the food supply and demand situation of North Korea and its policy implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

North Korea's food balance is very much affected by the availability and utilization of agricultural input factors and by the implementation of pro-military oriented or pro-market oriented economic policies.

the food supply and demand in North Korea can be improved by increasing the amount of agricultural resources, by decreasing the amount of pro-military oriented policies and by adopting a pro-market oriented economic reform.

the North Korean government should implement pro-market oriented economic policies to increase the rate of agricultural input factors and decrease the rate of population in order to meet the food needs of the average North Korean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a pro-market oriented economic approach is necessary for North Korea to recover its food balance, but it would be difficult for the North Korean government to implement a pro-market economic policy without first increasing its agricultural input factors.
the food balance in North Korea is not a result of a single factor, but rather a combination of factors including agricultural resources, policy, and population growth.
the North Korean economy is not self sufficient in terms of food production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the North Korean economy is a closed one and the food balance in North Korea is determined by agricultural resources and the economic policy of the regime.

the North Korean government must increase the rate of production of agricultural resources and must also implement a more pro-market oriented economic approach in order to meet the food demand of the North Korean people.
North Korea is not a self-sufficient country in food.
